newsitem.title: SURINAM: Angry Suriname pyramid investors loot supermarket.
newsitem.headline: Angry Suriname pyramid investors loot supermarket.

text.p: Dozens of angry Surinamese depositors who lost their money in the collapse of a pyramid banking scheme looted a supermarket owned by the man who took their money, police said on Friday.

The mob stormed the Roep NV Coppename supermarket in the South American capital on Thursday, tearing tins and packages from shelves and swigging from bottles of spirits and wine, a police spokesman said.
Four of the 40 to 50 looters were arrested but released hours later without being charged, he said.

It was the first report of looting since Roepsingh Ramtahalsingh, owner of Roep NV Coppename, announced earlier this month that he could not pay back depositors who had invested in a get-rich-quick scheme which promised interest rates of 120 percent. Commercial banks offer savings rates of about 20 percent.

Local economists said the collapse of Roep and similar saving schemes, which rely on ever increasing numbers of depositors to pay off old investors, has led to fears of widespread violence in the former Dutch colony of 430,000 people as occurred in Albania where similar schemes failed in April.
